channel.description: Latest articles from Wisconsin Public Radio (wpr.org)

item.title: Republicans send ‘400-year veto’ constitutional amendment to voters
item.description: Wisconsin voters will be asked whether the state's constitution should be amended to prevent the governor's powerful partial veto from increasing taxes or fees. The post Republicans send ‘400-year veto’ constitutional amendment to voters appeared first on WPR.

item.title: From undocumented to green cards: two sisters’ immigration journey
item.description: "Status Pending," a new podcast from WUWM, takes an in-depth look at what people experience when they go through the U.S. immigration system. The post From undocumented to green cards: two sisters’ immigration journey appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Wisconsin’s campus child care facilities offer parents foothold in higher education
item.description: "Wisconsin Today" spoke with the directors of two higher education child care centers about the needs of student-parents and the challenges they face when it comes to seeking child care and education. The post Wisconsin’s campus child care facilities offer parents foothold in higher education appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Fewer seasonal migrant workers apply for visas ahead of Wisconsin’s growing season
item.description: Federal officials announced that ICE agents are set to leave Minnesota after a months-long immigration crackdown. A Wisconsin business owner said the crackdown has stoked fear — and a Milwaukee nonprofit told WPR fewer agricultural workers are applying to work in Wisconsin. The post Fewer seasonal migrant workers apply for visas ahead of Wisconsin’s growing season appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Ho-Chunk elder channels inner rock ‘n’ roll teenager in new memoir
item.description: In “Bear Tracks,” Sherman Funmaker traces his journey from high school dropout to published writer. The post Ho-Chunk elder channels inner rock ‘n’ roll teenager in new memoir appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Bad River tribe wants court to halt construction of Enbridge’s Line 5 reroute
item.description: A northern Wisconsin tribe wants a court to halt construction of Enbridge’s $450 million plan to reroute an oil and gas pipeline around its reservation after an administrative law judge upheld state permits for the project. The post Bad River tribe wants court to halt construction of Enbridge’s Line 5 reroute appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Police in Wisconsin want to use facial recognition technology but face pushback
item.description: The Milwaukee Police Department and the Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office are among the Wisconsin law enforcement agencies exploring the use of facial recognition technology to help investigate crimes. The post Police in Wisconsin want to use facial recognition technology but face pushback appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Feds push back on former Judge Dugan’s attempts to overturn conviction
item.description: Federal prosecutors are pushing back on attempts by former Milwaukee County Judge Hannah Dugan to have her conviction overturned. Last year, a jury found her guilty of obstructing immigration agents. The post Feds push back on former Judge Dugan’s attempts to overturn conviction appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Wisconsin farmers wait to see how the end of Trump tariffs plays out
item.description: President Donald Trump's frequent use of tariffs over the last year has created plenty of economic uncertainty affecting Wisconsin farmers. But producers in the state say it's not clear what the end of the tariff policy will mean for them in the coming months. The post Wisconsin farmers wait to see how the end of Trump tariffs plays out appeared first on WPR.

item.title: Wisconsin Assembly passes deals on PFAS, SNAP funding
item.description: Capping off a contentious week of floor sessions that saw tempers flare as lawmakers raced to adjourn for the year, the state Assembly passed two measures tied to hard-fought deals about food assistance and cleaning up PFAS. The post Wisconsin Assembly passes deals on PFAS, SNAP funding appeared first on WPR.
